identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brabham BT62 track hypercar, in production from 2018, running the 5.4-litre Ford Modular V8 through a six-speed Holinger sequential manual gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: clutch-free move-off, automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies none of the three.
The source names a Holinger sequential but not its engagement, and the car provides its own blip, so no claim is made about whether a driver blip would otherwise be needed.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.brabham-bt62.20260816t034225128z-86c33ce9 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the BT62 and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source gives a 6-speed Holinger sequential manual, and the live drive selected six paddle gears with automatic cut and blip and no clutch needed to pull away.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
driver_summary: Six-speed Holinger sequential manual behind the 5.4-litre Ford Modular V8. Paddles, no clutch away from rest, and the car handles the cut and the blip.
